meta.title: Airbnb Almost Died In 2008. It Was Saved By Cereal.
meta.hook: Airbnb's founders once funded their struggling startup by selling presidential-election cereal for forty dollars a box.
meta.description: In 2008, before Airbnb was taking off, its founders were running low on money during the presidential election season. They designed novelty cereal boxes, 'Obama O's' and 'Cap'n McCain's,' selling roughly 500 of each at $40 a box. The stunt raised about $30,000, just enough runway to keep building the company that would later be valued in the billions.

scenes.narration: Airbnb's founders once funded their struggling startup by selling presidential-election cereal for forty dollars a box.

scenes.narration: During the two thousand eight campaign, they designed Obama O's and Cap'n McCain's as limited-edition collectibles.

visual.decision_reason: the literal, specific detail that makes the hook credible

scenes.narration: They assembled boxes by hand, filled them with ordinary cereal, and pitched the stunt to political-event crowds.

visual.visual_intent: Novelty cereal boxes lined up on a simple shelf, studio lighting, product-style shot
visual.decision_reason: sourced from Benzinga/CNBC business press reporting on the campaign

scenes.narration: The sales generated about thirty thousand dollars, according to co-founder Brian Chesky's account of the episode.

visual.decision_reason: the exact figure, corroborated across multiple outlets

scenes.narration: Cereal did not prove the home-sharing model, but it supplied cash and demonstrated the founders could create demand from almost nothing.

scenes.narration: Investors later used the boxes as evidence of resourcefulness. Before Airbnb scaled rooms, it sold a story in a cereal aisle.
